thread:
maria (PM): Quick sync — post-workshop notes attached. Need a tight set of objection handlers for procurement teams comparing Redwood's Dedicated/Private to cloud managed endpoints. Focus: predictable spend, SLOs, and compliance.
josh (growth): happy to help. can we keep each handler to 1-2 lines + a single supporting stat or link? helps SDRs.
anya (product marketing): yes — short claim, proof nugget, suggested soundbite. I'm drafting 6.
ben (solutions): common procurement objection: 'we can just use cloud provider endpoints, cheaper w/ sustained discounts' -> handler: 'public clouds show price volatility by instance and egress; Redwood Dedicated allows committed unit economics and predictable token pricing for steady workloads.' proof: 'case: fintech customer reduced unexpected monthly surges by 28% using reserved pools.'
kyle (sales): include SLO fallback point — buyers always ask about outages.
anya (product marketing): handler for reliability: 'Redwood routes automatically to compatible model variants and capacity tiers with circuit-breaker fallbacks to keep APIs online.' proof: '99.95% monthly uptime target on Dedicated + multi-region routing.' soundbite: "We bake graceful degradation into serving so your feature doesn't drop offline."
maria (PM): good. add a short technical appendix line for legal/compliance: KMS + audit logs + customer-controlled VPC. one line each.
ben (solutions): procurement loves specifics. For costs, show a simple math snippet: ```Committed capacity = reserved GPUs + monthly token throughput -> predictable unit cost = $X / 1M tokens``` keep X as placeholder for field teams.
josh (growth): can we get a one-slide benchmark comparison vs two cloud providers and one LLM API vendor? 3 axes: latency SLO, $/1M tokens at median seq=512, failover time.
maria (PM): yes — design will be 1 slide and 1-page battlecard. anya you own the deck copy, ben you own the appendix numbers, kyle owns the objection playbook for SDRs.
anya (product marketing): drafting language now. will push to /drive/marketing/competitive/objection-handlers-v1.pdf by EOD. launch-bot: New asset uploaded: /drive/marketing/competitive/objection-handlers-v1.pdf :paperclip:
kyle (sales): I'll run a quick roleplay with SDRs tomorrow. can someone give me 3 quick one-liners for cold outreach that mention "predictable spend" without sounding like pricing talk?
anya (product marketing): 1) "Swap surprise cloud bills for predictable, committed inference capacity." 2) "Built for steady production — predictable token economics, not surprise spikes." 3) "Deploy privately or hosted — same SLOs, no sticker shock."
josh (growth): :thumbsup: these are solid. Add AB test variants: talk about latency in variant B.
maria (PM): great progress. final ask: everyone thumbs up on the slide copy by 11am tomorrow. otherwise I'll merge and tag ops for numbers. :calendar:
